items.title: Scalar finite-element substructuring model
items.statement:
Fix a bounded, connected polygonal open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^2$ with a nonempty Dirichlet boundary segment. A finite **subdomain partition** is a family of connected polygonal open sets $Ω_i$, $1\le i\le N$, whose closures cover $\overline\Omega$, whose interiors are disjoint, and for which $\overline\Omega_i\cap\overline\Omega_j$ ($i\ne j$) is a whole common side, a common vertex, or empty. The outer Dirichlet segment is a union of mesh boundary sides. The edge-adjacency graph of each triangulated subdomain is connected, and the subdomain adjacency graph is connected to the Dirichlet boundary. Each subdomain has a matching affine simplicial triangulation; the triangulations match on every shared side. The family has a fixed shape-regularity bound, quasiuniform mesh size $h_i$, uniformly bounded polygon side count, corner angles bounded below, inradius comparable to $H_i$, and a uniform interior-cone parameter. Write $H_i=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega_i)$ and $H/h=\max_i H_i/h_i$.

Use continuous piecewise-affine ($P_1$) scalar functions on each triangulation. The reference-element and face-matching conventions are those of [[def-reference-finite-element-and-unisolvent-dofs]], [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], and [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]: local polynomials are affine, their nodal values determine them, and conforming functions have equal traces across a shared side. For each subdomain choose a coefficient $\rho_i>0$, constant on $\Omega_i$ but allowed to jump across interfaces. Its local energy is

$$a_i(v,w)=\rho_i\sum_{K\subset\Omega_i}\int_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx.$$

The global finite-element space consists of the continuous piecewise-affine functions on the subdomain meshes that vanish on the outer Dirichlet boundary, with energy $a(v,w)=\sum_i a_i(v|_{\Omega_i},w|_{\Omega_i})$. Local interior degrees of freedom are the mesh vertices strictly inside $\Omega_i$; local boundary degrees of freedom are its remaining vertices, with outer Dirichlet values fixed to zero. A **floating local block** means the same local energy before any outer-boundary values are fixed. A **subdomain corner** is a vertex of its polygonal boundary.

For uniform estimates, the fixed polygon-shape parameters include the scaled Lipschitz character: after rescaling each subdomain to diameter one, its boundary has a graph-chart cover with uniformly bounded chart count and Lipschitz constants and a uniformly positive neighborhood radius. The scaled mean-zero Poincaré constants are also included among these fixed shape parameters. A pointwise interior-cone bound alone is not a substitute for this uniform boundary-chart data. All constants in later two-dimensional estimates may depend on these polygon-shape, side-count, and mesh shape-regularity bounds, but not on $h$, $H$, the number of subdomains, or the positive numbers $\rho_i$.

references.title: Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 35–37, 83–89
Oliver Rheinbach, Parallel Scalable Iterative Substructuring, Chapter 2, §§2.1–2.4

items.title: Eigenvalue bounds from a left-inverse preconditioner
items.statement:
Let $A:V\to V'$ be symmetric positive definite on a finite-dimensional real vector space, and let $L:V\to U$, $T:U\to V$ satisfy $LT=I_U$. Every eigenvalue of

$$G=(LA^{-1}L^T)(T^TAT)$$

lies in $[1,\|TL\|_A^2]$, where $\|Q\|_A:=\sup_{v\ne0}\sqrt{\langle A Qv,Qv\rangle/\langle Av,v\rangle}$. When $V=\{0\}$, set $\|Q\|_A=0$ for its unique endomorphism. In that case $LT=I_U$ forces $U=\{0\}$, the spectrum of $G$ is empty, and the eigenvalue assertion is vacuous.

references.title: Jan Mandel and Bedřich Sousedík, BDDC and FETI-DP under Minimalist Assumptions, §4, Lemma 4.1
Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 94–95

items.title: Floating local kernels and positive interior blocks
items.statement: In the setting of [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]], the nullspace of the floating local energy matrix on a connected $\Omega_i$ is exactly the one-dimensional space of constants. The principal stiffness block $K_{II}^{(i)}$ on interior nodal values with zero boundary trace is positive definite (including the empty $0$-dimensional block convention). The assembled global Dirichlet stiffness matrix is positive definite.

references.title: Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 35–37 and 83–84
Oliver Rheinbach, Parallel Scalable Iterative Substructuring, Chapter 2, §§2.1–2.3

items.title: Primal interface spaces and jump convention
items.statement:
For each $i$, let $W_i$ be the vector space of local boundary nodal traces compatible with the fixed outer Dirichlet values, and set $W=\prod_i W_i$ (all interface copies independent). Let $\widehat W\subset W$ be the subspace whose nodal traces agree at every shared interface node; let $R:\widehat W\to W$ be the inclusion. Choose a set of **primal constraints**, meaning finitely many linear functionals on local traces whose values are required to agree across their incident subdomains. Vertex values and normalized edge averages are examples. The **partially assembled space** $\widetilde W$ is the subspace of $W$ satisfying those primal equalities, so $\widehat W\subset\widetilde W\subset W$.

The remaining continuity equations are collected in a jump map $B:\widetilde W\to\mathbb R^m$ with $\ker B=\widehat W$. It may contain redundant rows. Fix the **redundant-multiplier convention** $\Lambda:=\operatorname{range}B$ with its inherited Euclidean inner product: multiplier vectors are elements of this range, not arbitrary row-coordinate vectors modulo an unstated choice. Then $B^T$ is injective on $\Lambda$. For the PE26 two-dimensional estimate, all subdomain vertices are primal and the only remaining jump rows are nodal differences on open interface edges, each shared by exactly two subdomains.

An interface corner is primal whenever its value is among the selected primal functionals. An **edge average** on a side $E$ is $|E|^{-1}\int_E v_h\,ds$, which is a finite sum of nodal values for a $P_1$ trace. The two-dimensional bound below uses corner constraints; no edge-average bound is claimed there.

references.title: Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 83–89
Jan Mandel and Bedřich Sousedík, BDDC and FETI-DP under Minimalist Assumptions, §3.1

items.title: Discrete harmonic extension and interface Schur complement
items.statement:
Use the interior/interface ordering of [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]]. The boundary-trace spaces $W_i$, $W=\prod_iW_i$, the conforming space $\widehat W$, the partially assembled space $\widetilde W$, and the inclusion $R:\widehat W\to W$ are those of [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]]. In particular, $R$ identifies the copies of a conforming interface trace. In subdomain $i$, write its stiffness matrix as

$$K_i=\begin{pmatrix}K_{II}^{(i)}&K_{I\Gamma}^{(i)}\\K_{\Gamma I}^{(i)}&K_{\Gamma\Gamma}^{(i)}\end{pmatrix}.$$

By [[thm-pe26-local-energy-kernel-and-interior-spd]], $K_{II}^{(i)}$ is positive definite when nonempty; on the zero-dimensional interior space its unique endomorphism is invertible. For admissible boundary trace $g_i$, the **discrete harmonic extension** is

$$H_i g_i:=\begin{pmatrix}-(K_{II}^{(i)})^{-1}K_{I\Gamma}^{(i)}g_i\\g_i\end{pmatrix}.$$

The local **interface Schur complement** is

$$S_i:=K_{\Gamma\Gamma}^{(i)}-K_{\Gamma I}^{(i)}(K_{II}^{(i)})^{-1}K_{I\Gamma}^{(i)}.$$

This is the Schur complement in [[def-block-lu-factorisation]]. The local Schur form on a trace is $g_i^TS_i g_i$. The block identity and the associated block LU factorization use [[thm-block-lu-factorisation-via-an-invertible-leading-block]] with leading block $K_{II}^{(i)}$. Assembling local Schur forms on $\widehat W$ gives $\widehat S=R^T(\operatorname{diag}_i S_i)R$; restricting the same block-diagonal form to $\widetilde W$ gives the partially assembled operator $\widetilde S$.

references.title: Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 35–37
Oliver Rheinbach, Parallel Scalable Iterative Substructuring, Chapter 2, §§2.1–2.3

items.title: Primal constraints remove local floating kernels
items.statement: Assume the hypotheses of [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and the energy setting of [[thm-pe26-local-energy-kernel-and-interior-spd]]. If each floating local component has at least one primal vertex value fixed in its dual subproblem, its local dual stiffness is positive definite. If all subdomain vertices are primal and the global Dirichlet boundary is nonempty, the partially assembled interface energy is positive definite; hence the BDDC and FETI-DP exact local and coarse solves are well-defined.

references.title: Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 83–86
Oliver Rheinbach, Parallel Scalable Iterative Substructuring, Chapter 2, §§2.1–2.3

items.title: Discrete harmonic extension minimizes energy
items.statement: For every admissible local trace $g_i$, $H_i g_i$ from [[def-pe26-discrete-harmonic-extension-and-schur-complement]] is the unique finite-element function with trace $g_i$ minimizing $a_i(v,v)$. The minimum is $g_i^TS_i g_i$.

references.title: Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 35–37
Oliver Rheinbach, Parallel Scalable Iterative Substructuring, Chapter 2, §§2.1–2.3

items.title: Static condensation is the exact interface problem
items.statement:
Let $f_i=(f_I^{(i)},f_\Gamma^{(i)})^T$ be local load contributions whose assembly is the global Galerkin load. For the global conforming Dirichlet finite-element system from [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]], eliminating all subdomain interior variables gives the assembled interface Schur system. Its solution trace is exactly the trace of the unique global Galerkin solution. After solving for this trace, reconstruct each local interior vector by

$$u_I^{(i)}=(K_{II}^{(i)})^{-1}(f_I^{(i)}-K_{I\Gamma}^{(i)}u_\Gamma^{(i)}).$$

These interior values recover the unique global Galerkin solution; the trace-dependent homogeneous part of each local reconstruction is the discrete harmonic extension.

references.title: Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 35–37
Jan Mandel and Bedřich Sousedík, BDDC and FETI-DP under Minimalist Assumptions, §5

items.title: Coefficient-scaled averaging and BDDC
items.statement:
Use the spaces and partial Schur operator of [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and [[def-pe26-discrete-harmonic-extension-and-schur-complement]]. Let $E_0:\widetilde W\to\widehat W$ average every remaining interface degree of freedom and preserve every already-shared primal value. It is a scaled average if the weights for all copies of each such degree of freedom sum to one. Put $\bar E:=R E_0:\widetilde W\to\widetilde W$. Then $E_0R=I_{\widehat W}$ and $\bar E$ is a projection onto $\widehat W$.

In the PE26 two-dimensional corner-constraint branch, each non-primal node is interior to one interface edge shared by exactly two subdomains $i,j$. Set

$$ (E_0w)(x)=\frac{\rho_i}{\rho_i+\rho_j}w_i(x)+\frac{\rho_j}{\rho_i+\rho_j}w_j(x). $$

At primal nodes the copies already agree, so the average is the common value. For any finite-dimensional positive definite partial Schur operator $\widetilde S$, the **BDDC preconditioner** is

$$M_{\rm BDDC}^{-1}:=E_0\widetilde S^{-1}E_0^T:\widehat W'\to\widehat W,$$

for the assembled interface system with operator $\widehat S=R^T\widetilde S R$. Its constrained partial-energy interpretation is established in [[prop-pe26-bddc-constrained-local-minimization]].

references.title: Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 87–90 and 96–97
Jan Mandel and Bedřich Sousedík, BDDC and FETI-DP under Minimalist Assumptions, §§3.1–3.2

items.title: Discrete Schur energy and the fractional trace norm
items.statement:
Let $\Omega_i$ be one of the shape-regular polygonal subdomains in [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]], with a matching quasiuniform $P_1$ mesh. For any continuous piecewise-linear boundary trace $g$, let $S_i^{\rm fl}$ be the Schur complement of the floating local stiffness matrix, before outer Dirichlet values are fixed, formed by the same interior elimination as in [[def-pe26-discrete-harmonic-extension-and-schur-complement]]. Define

$$|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}^2:=\int_{\partial\Omega_i}\int_{\partial\Omega_i}\frac{|g(s)-g(t)|^2}{|s-t|^2}\,ds\,dt.$$

This seminorm is taken modulo constants. The floating local Schur energy satisfies

$$c\rho_i|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}^2\le g^TS_i^{\rm fl} g\le C\rho_i|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}^2,$$

where $c,C>0$ depend only on the fixed scaled polygon-shape parameters (including boundary-chart and mean-zero Poincaré bounds), mesh shape-regularity and quasiuniformity. The upper bound is realized by a boundary-preserving finite-element lifting; the minimum-energy lifting is the floating discrete harmonic extension. For an admissible trace $g$, whose outer Dirichlet values are zero, $g^TS_i^{\rm fl}g=g^TS_i g$ for the Dirichlet-restricted Schur matrix of [[def-pe26-discrete-harmonic-extension-and-schur-complement]], so the same inequalities hold for that matrix on its domain.

references.title: Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 24–26
Oliver Rheinbach, Parallel Scalable Iterative Substructuring, Chapter 1 §1.7 and Chapter 2 §2.4

items.title: BDDC is the constrained partial-energy minimizer
items.statement:
For every assembled residual $f\in\widehat W'$, the unique minimizer over $w\in\widetilde W$ of

$$J_f(w)=\tfrac12\langle\widetilde S w,w\rangle-\langle f,E_0w\rangle$$

is $w_* = \widetilde S^{-1}E_0^T f$. The conforming correction returned by BDDC is $E_0 w_*=E_0\widetilde S^{-1}E_0^T f$.

references.title: Jan Mandel and Bedřich Sousedík, BDDC and FETI-DP under Minimalist Assumptions, §3.2
Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, §§87–88

items.title: FETI-DP dual system and preconditioner
items.statement:
Use $\widetilde W$, $\widehat W$, $E_0$, $R$, $B$ and $\Lambda=\operatorname{range}B$ as defined in [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and [[def-pe26-scaled-averaging-and-bddc-preconditioner]]. Assume that $\widetilde S:\widetilde W\to\widetilde W'$ is symmetric positive definite. In the PE26 corner branch this follows from [[thm-pe26-primal-constraints-remove-floating-kernels]] when all subdomain vertices are primal and the global Dirichlet boundary is nonempty; for other primal choices it is a separate admissibility requirement. Use the inherited Euclidean inner product to identify $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda'$ in the transpose and coordinate formulas below. Regard $\bar E=R E_0$ as a projection on $\widetilde W$. Since $\ker B=\operatorname{range}\bar E=\widehat W$, each class of traces with the same jump has a unique representative in $\ker\bar E$. Define $B_D^T:\Lambda\to\widetilde W$ by assigning to $\lambda\in\Lambda$ that unique representative $w$ with $Bw=\lambda$ and $\bar Ew=0$. This is the scaled right inverse; it obeys $BB_D^T=I_\Lambda$ and $B_D^TB=I_{\widetilde W}-\bar E$. The latter identity makes the primal and dual projections complementary. In the two-subdomain edge case, its two entries are the coefficient-scaled jump weights complementary to those in $E_0$.

The **FETI-DP dual operator** and its preconditioner are

$$F:=B\widetilde S^{-1}B^T:\Lambda\to\Lambda',\qquad M_{\rm FETI-DP}^{-1}:=B_D\widetilde S B_D^T:\Lambda'\to\Lambda.$$

The multiplier convention removes dependent row coordinates: $\lambda$ is in $\operatorname{range}B$, so no arbitrary multiplier component in $\ker B^T$ is retained. Elimination of the partially assembled displacement and the resulting exact dual system are proved in [[prop-pe26-feti-dp-is-dual-schur-complement]].

references.title: Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, §§83–90
Jan Mandel and Bedřich Sousedík, BDDC and FETI-DP under Minimalist Assumptions, §§3.1 and 3.3

items.title: Two-dimensional logarithmic edge cutoff estimates
items.statement:
Let $E$ be a side of a shape-regular polygon of diameter $H$ with a matching quasiuniform $P_1$ boundary mesh of size $h$. Let $\theta_E$ be the piecewise-linear boundary function equal to $1$ at the interior nodes of $E$ and $0$ at the endpoints and all other boundary nodes. For

$$\|q\|_{00,E}^2:=\int_E\int_E\frac{|q(s)-q(t)|^2}{|s-t|^2}\,ds\,dt+\int_E\frac{|q(s)|^2}{\operatorname{dist}(s,\partial E)}\,ds,$$

one has $\|\theta_E\|_{00,E}^2\le C(1+\log(H/h))$. Also every continuous piecewise-affine $u_h$ on $\Omega_i$ satisfies

$$\|u_h-\overline u_{\Omega_i}\|_{L^\infty(\Omega_i)}^2\le C(1+\log(H_i/h_i))\|\nabla u_h\|_{L^2(\Omega_i)}^2.$$

Consequently, for the edge mean $\overline u_E$,

$$\|I_h(\theta_E(u_h-\overline u_E))\|_{00,E}^2\le C(1+\log(H_i/h_i))^2\|\nabla u_h\|_{L^2(\Omega_i)}^2,$$

where $I_h$ is nodal piecewise-linear interpolation on $E$.

references.title: Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 25–33
references.locator: printed pp. 30–33, estimate (5) and its proof: the two-dimensional finite-element Sobolev inequality

references.title: Oliver Rheinbach, Parallel Scalable Iterative Substructuring, Chapter 2 §2.4, pp. 40–44

items.title: FETI-DP is the exact dual Schur system
items.statement:
Let $f\in\widehat W'$ and set $\widetilde f=E_0^T f$. The constrained minimization problem

$$\min_{w\in\widetilde W,\ Bw=0}\left(\tfrac12\langle\widetilde S w,w\rangle-\langle\widetilde f,w\rangle\right)$$

has the saddle equations $\widetilde S w+B^T\lambda=\widetilde f$, $Bw=0$. Eliminating $w$ gives the FETI-DP dual system

$$B\widetilde S^{-1}B^T\lambda=B\widetilde S^{-1}E_0^Tf.$$

On $\Lambda=\operatorname{range}B$ its matrix is positive definite, and the exact multiplier solution reconstructs the unique assembled interface solution $w\in\widehat W$.

references.title: Jan Mandel and Bedřich Sousedík, BDDC and FETI-DP under Minimalist Assumptions, §3.3
Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, §§83–84 and 89

items.title: Complementary primal and dual projections share nonunit spectrum
items.statement:
Let $V,U_1,U_2$ be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let $A:V\to V'$ be symmetric positive definite, and let $L_i:V\to U_i$, $T_i:U_i\to V$ satisfy $L_iT_i=I_{U_i}$ for $i=1,2$ and $T_1L_1+T_2L_2=I_V$. Then the operators

$$G_1=(L_1A^{-1}L_1^T)(T_1^TAT_1),\qquad G_2=(T_2^TAT_2)(L_2A^{-1}L_2^T)$$

have the same eigenvalues, with the same multiplicities, except possibly at the eigenvalue $1$.

references.title: Jan Mandel and Bedřich Sousedík, BDDC and FETI-DP under Minimalist Assumptions, §4, Lemmas 4.1–4.2
Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 90–93

items.title: Two-dimensional scaled averaging energy bound
items.statement:
Assume the model of [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]], all subdomain vertices primal, and the coefficient-scaled average of [[def-pe26-scaled-averaging-and-bddc-preconditioner]]. Let $P:=I-R E_0$ be the complementary jump projection on $\widetilde W$, and let $\|\cdot\|_{\widetilde S}$ be the energy norm induced by the partially assembled Schur operator. Then

$$\|Pw\|_{\widetilde S}^2\le C(1+\log(H/h))^2\|w\|_{\widetilde S}^2\qquad(w\in\widetilde W),$$

where $C$ depends only on the polygon/mesh shape bounds and bounded side count. It is independent of coefficient jumps, mesh size, subdomain diameter, and subdomain count.

references.title: Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 94–97
Oliver Rheinbach, Parallel Scalable Iterative Substructuring, Chapter 2 §2.4, pp. 39–44

items.title: Conditioning and solver work are separate claims
items.statement: The condition-number estimate controls ideal preconditioned iteration counts, not total work; local and coarse factorization costs depend on solver choices and coarse dimension.

references.title: Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 3 and 87–89

items.title: BDDC and FETI-DP have matching nontrivial spectra
items.statement: For BDDC and FETI-DP built from the same positive definite partially assembled Schur operator, primal constraints, and scaled averaging, all eigenvalues of the two preconditioned operators other than $1$ agree with multiplicity. With the multiplier space fixed as $\Lambda=\operatorname{range}B$, neither operator has a zero eigenvalue; retaining all redundant row coordinates instead would add only multiplier null modes that are removed by this convention. The multiplicity of $1$ is not asserted to agree.

references.title: Jan Mandel and Bedřich Sousedík, BDDC and FETI-DP under Minimalist Assumptions, §4
Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 90–93

items.title: The two-dimensional BDDC and FETI-DP polylogarithmic bound
items.statement:
Assume the scalar model of [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]], matching shape-regular quasiuniform $P_1$ meshes on bounded-shape polygonal subdomains in two dimensions, all subdomain vertices primal, coefficient scaling $\rho_i/(\rho_i+\rho_j)$ on each open interface edge, and nonzero assembled and multiplier spaces. Then both preconditioned interface operators satisfy

$$\kappa(M_{\rm BDDC}^{-1}\widehat S)\le C(1+\log(H/h))^2,\qquad \kappa(M_{\rm FETI-DP}^{-1}F)\le C(1+\log(H/h))^2.$$

The constant is independent of $h$, $H$, the number of subdomains, and arbitrary positive jumps in the coefficient values $\rho_i$. If either preconditioned space is zero-dimensional, that interface solve is trivial and its condition number is not asserted. This statement does not cover three-dimensional vertex-only constraints, arbitrary graph or mesh geometries, or unaligned/intra-subdomain high-contrast coefficients.

references.title: Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 94–97
Oliver Rheinbach, Parallel Scalable Iterative Substructuring, Chapter 2 §2.4, Theorems 2.4.1–2.4.3
Jan Mandel and Bedřich Sousedík, BDDC and FETI-DP under Minimalist Assumptions, §4

items.title: A floating component without a constant-detecting primal constraint remains singular
items.statement:
For a floating square subdomain with the local matrix

$$K=\tfrac12\begin{pmatrix}2&-1&0&-1\\-1&2&-1&0\\0&-1&2&-1\\-1&0&-1&2\end{pmatrix},$$

suppose no corner value (and no other functional that detects constants) is primal on that component. Its local energy matrix still has the constant vector in its kernel, so the local dual solve is singular. Omitting one corner while another corner remains primal does not produce this counterexample; the failure is the absence of any local anchor.

references.title: Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 83–86

items.title: Two floating Poisson subdomains and primal anchoring
items.statement:
Take two adjacent unit-square subdomains, each split by the diagonal from its southwest to its northeast corner into two affine triangles, and put coefficient $\rho=1$. Before outer Dirichlet values are imposed, each local floating stiffness matrix in the cyclic vertex order $(a,b,c,d)$ is

$$K_i=\tfrac12\begin{pmatrix}2&-1&0&-1\\-1&2&-1&0\\0&-1&2&-1\\-1&0&-1&2\end{pmatrix}.$$

The two interface endpoints are primal corners. Impose homogeneous Dirichlet data on the full top exterior side of the two-square domain, a nonempty segment that is a union of mesh sides. The local constant modes are thereby anchored, and the shared primal corners enforce their common interface values; after exact interior elimination, the assembled Schur solve is the original finite-element problem.

references.title: Olof B. Widlund, Introduction to the Design and Theory of Domain Decomposition Algorithms, DD20 Tutorial, pp. 35–37 and 83–84

items.title: A finite-dimensional BDDC/FETI-DP spectral match
items.statement: Let $\widetilde W=\mathbb R^2$, $\widetilde S=A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$, $\widehat W=\operatorname{span}(e_1)$, $R=e_1$, $E_0=(1\;0)$, $B=(0\;1)$, and $B_D^T=e_2$. Then $E_0R=1$, $BB_D^T=1$, and $R E_0+B_D^TB=I$. The single BDDC and FETI-DP preconditioned eigenvalues both equal $4/3$.

references.title: Jan Mandel and Bedřich Sousedík, BDDC and FETI-DP under Minimalist Assumptions, §§3–4

items.title: A dense coarse solve can dominate local work
items.statement: Assume all hypotheses of [[thm-pe26-condition-number-2d-polylogarithmic]]: the two-dimensional scalar model, matching shape-regular quasiuniform meshes with fixed polygon-shape bounds, positive coefficients constant on subdomains, all subdomain vertices primal, coefficient-scaled averaging, and nonzero assembled and multiplier spaces. Consider a dense direct-solve cost model for the resulting positive definite local dual and coarse blocks with $N$ subdomains, local matrix dimension $m$ fixed, and a coarse dimension $n_c$ proportional to $N$. If local matrices are factored concurrently by dense Cholesky, the local arithmetic is $O(Nm^3)$ in total and $O(m^3)$ ideal parallel time. The coarse factorization uses $O(n_c^3)$ arithmetic and $O(n_c^2)$ storage. For fixed $H/h$, [[thm-pe26-condition-number-2d-polylogarithmic]] keeps the iteration condition bound independent of $N$, while the dense coarse solve can dominate total work.
